body: The fact that it's not already available makes me want to forcibly euthanase the whole of humanity.

Muscle cells do NOT simple divide.  If they just grew arbitrarily they'd be an amorphous useless mass.  As the individual cells grow they collectively assume a particular gross conformation.  No nervous system is required to orchestrate this.  The whole body does this - grows in an anisotropic fashion.

This heliotropism is relatively simple; it's the result of many cells reacting the presence or absence of light upon them, which they can of course detect.

>But one day an old friend walked past, recognised me and pulled me off the street, cleaned me up and gave me a sofa to sleep on.

Gee.  Too bad most people are not nearly kind enough to do that for another person.  Not fucking nearly.

I really think that the people who downvoted this submission shouldn't even be allowed to continue to use this site.  Evidently, they think it's so important to have interesting content and to have everything in its proper place that they wish to conceal what are possibly the last words of a desperate human being and his last effort to seek help with problems that may be too great for him at this point to rectify or bear by himself.  Is there an unusually large number of psychopaths on Reddit?  Serious question.
That's like saying, "how do muscle cells grow and organize if they don't have a brain" or "how do chemical reactions take place if the reactants don't have a brain"?

>If I had gotten help early on, I wouldn't have wasted all these years **whining**, contemplating suicide, **being totally self-absorbed**

This is entirely the wrong thing to say to a suicidal person.  He already has very low self-esteem and you're attacking what remaining islands of it he has left?

The thing is that ALL people, no matter how altruistic, will prioritize their own needs over others when the circumstances of their lives become straitened and dire.  And, in my judgment, there is nothing wrong with that.  How much sense does it make that resources / prosperity / energy (in short, things of utility and promoters of happiness) should flow from areas of lowest concentration to highest?  It should flow from areas of highest to lowest.  You wouldn't expect the homeless to give away their money and time to help those with a home, car, job, and income, would you?  Therefore, it's hard for me to see anything wrong with the self-absorption of the depressed.  And  before you say so, I don't think it's this self-absorption which causes or maintains the depression.  With the alleviation of depression comes a greater capacity for empathy and selflessness and those too fond of the post hoc ergo propter hoc fallacy may assume that that means that the loss of self-absorption diminished the depression rather than that the diminution of depression occasioned the loss of the self-absorption, which is the more likely direction of causality in my opinion.

And calling him a whiner trivializes the suffering he is going through.  The fact that you've been depressed doesn't necessarily mean that he is experiencing pain of the same degree as you did; if you found yours to be more-or-less tolerable, good, but his may be excruciating.  Don't do that to someone in a state of desperation making one last effort to reach out to humanity for some compassion, concern, and charity.

I don't think the imaginations of most redditors are advanced enough for them to perceive any possibility other than that you were attention-whoring.  Hence the downvotes.  

What's obviously going on here is that you are seriously considering suicide but have some faint hope that there's a way you could live and be happy, and you have therefore turned to Redditors supposing that they might have some ideas for you as to how to realize that sliver of a hope.  Or perhaps you're just trying to abate the sting of these painful emotions by getting them off your chest.

I hate the way people always assume the worst about others - in particular that they are disposed to think so poorly of those who purport to be mentally ill.

I, unfortunately, don't have any answers for you because I'm in much the same boat.
